婿.meaning: A <part>woman</part> waits at the altar under a full <part>moon</part>. Her nervous groom arrives late and hopping, one foot jammed in a <part>giant boot</part> he grabbed in a panic from the costume shop. The guests cheer anyway: here comes the <kanji>bridegroom</kanji>.
婿.on: The rings are locked in a steel <sound>Sa</sound>fe, and he has forgotten the code.
婿.kun: The best man, a <sound>moo</sound>se, holds the ring on one antler while a <sound>ko</sound>ala tugs the giant boot off.

哲.meaning: A barber can't keep his <part>mouth</part> shut: snipping away, he asks why hair grows back and who we would be if we were bald. He gives each cut lock a careful <part>fold</part> into a paper packet, 'to think about later'. One haircut, two hours of <kanji>philosophy</kanji>.
哲.on: A tiny <sound>tet</sound>ra fish in his shop tank stares back, as if it is thinking too.
哲.kun: His sharpest customer, a <sound>sa</sound>rdine seller, taps the <sound>to</sound>p of the barber's head and says an <sound>ea</sound>gle has more hair: clever.

槽.meaning: In a forest <part>office</part>, the staff hollow out a fallen <part>tree</part> and fill it with coffee, so nobody has to walk to the kitchen. All day, mugs dip in from every desk at once: the office <kanji>vat</kanji>.
槽.on: Someone drops a bar of <sound>so</sound>ap in by mistake, and the coffee foams for a week.
槽.kun: The intern naps on a <sound>fu</sound>ton beside it, holding a <sound>ne</sound>t to fish the soap out.

拙.meaning: A pirate tries to leave port in style. He swings the <part>anchor</part> up with a flourish, and it smashes the harbour's <part>exit</part> sign, then lands on his own toe. The crew just sighs: their captain is famously <kanji>bungling</kanji>.
拙.on: His <sound>set</sound>ter dog has to steer the ship home.
拙.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' he sneezes, knocking a <sound>ta</sound>co off the rail, and the <sound>na</sound>chos follow it overboard.

綿.meaning: Besieged in her castle, a grandma finds there's no white cloth left to surrender with. So she picks fluffy bolls in the courtyard, spins <part>thread</part> and weaves a <part>white flag</part>. The enemy is so taken with its softness that they ask where she grows her <kanji>cotton</kanji>.
綿.on: Peace is signed, and the enemy general orders from her <sound>men</sound>u of socks.
綿.kun: His baby goes '<sound>Wah</sound>!' until grandma gives her a fluffy toy shaped like a jam <sound>ta</sound>rt.

峡.meaning: On a ledge between steep <part>mountain</part> walls, three hikers meet a goat coming the other way. The only way past is a tight <part>group hug</part>, goat included, shuffling sideways over the drop. Far below, a river roars through the <kanji>gorge</kanji>.
峡.on: A hiker reads the goat's collar tag aloud, stretching the start so it echoes off the walls: '<sound>Kyo</sound>to!'
峡.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' bleats the goat, and trots off to the ba<sound>za</sound>ar on the far side to find its <sound>ma</sound>ma.

秩.meaning: A farmer plants her <part>grain</part> in perfect rows, one stalk per step. When a single stalk goes missing, she'd rather <part>lose</part> the whole field than leave a gap, so she replants it at midnight with a ruler. Her farm runs on strict <kanji>regularity</kanji>.
秩.on: Each row is guarded by a <sound>chee</sound>tah that sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' at every crow.

羅.meaning: A beekeeper makes her own veil. She unpicks an old fishing <part>net</part> and reweaves each <part>fiber</part> finer and finer, until bees can't get through but sunlight can. It floats over her hat like a cloud of <kanji>gauze</kanji>.
羅.on: Her bees buzz around her like cheerleaders: '<sound>Rah</sound>!'
羅.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>ps,' she says, as a bee lands on her <sound>su</sound>shi; a <sound>mo</sound>th taps the veil, and she whispers, '<sound>No</sound>t you either.'

賄.meaning: In a beach court, a crab on trial slides a pearl-filled <part>shellfish</part> under the seagull judge's wing. Eager to <part>possess</part> that pearl, the gull bangs his gavel: not guilty! Every crab on the sand saw the <kanji>bribe</kanji>.
賄.on: '<sound>Why</sound>?' squawks a second gull, who wanted a pearl too.
賄.kun: The crab's <sound>ma</sound>ma pays the court fees, <sound>ca</sound>lmly counting out <sound>na</sound>chos, then drops one: '<sound>Oo</sound>ps.' She provides for everything.

塾.meaning: After school the kids want a <part>ball game</part>, but their parents send them down to a classroom dug into the <part>soil</part> under the playground, doing sums till nine. Above them, the ball bounces alone. That basement is the <kanji>cram school</kanji>.
塾.on: A <sound>ju</sound>ry of moles marks their tests and hands out one <sound>coo</sound>kie each.

懲.meaning: In the cat court, the goldfish thief must sit in the window wearing a <part>sign</part> that says 'I ate the goldfish', his little <part>heart</part> sinking every time a bird laughs. Cat law is strict, and its <kanji>penal</kanji> code is very public.
懲.on: The sign hangs from a tight <sound>cho</sound>ker of jingling bells.
懲.kun: Next day he walks past the <sound>ko</sound>i pond and its <sound>ree</sound>ds without one glance: lesson learned.

掌.meaning: At the bakery awards, the judge holds the winning bun up high on one flat <part>hand</part>, like a waiter with a tray: the cake held in the greatest <part>esteem</part>. Warm crumbs gather in the hollow of her <kanji>palm</kanji>.
掌.on: Then she bows to the crowd: the bun is the star of the <sound>show</sound>.
掌.kun: A <sound>te</sound>nnis fan bumps her ('Oh, <sound>no</sound>t again!'), and the bun bounces off a <sound>hee</sound>l into a bowl of <sound>ra</sound>men.

阪.meaning: Climbers race to plant their <part>pennant</part> on the hilltop, but a grumpy goat is <part>anti</part> visitors and butts each one back down. Only the slowest climber, who brought carrots, reaches the <kanji>heights</kanji>.
阪.on: The goat likes its carrots dipped in <sound>hon</sound>ey.
阪.kun: The fastest climber rolls back down the slope, past a <sound>sa</sound>lsa stall, and stops against a parked <sound>ca</sound>r.

雅.meaning: A huge walrus with one chipped <part>tusk</part> lets a <part>sparrow</part> hop onto it, then bows like a butler and offers it a crumb. The tiny bird bows back. Even a walrus can be <kanji>gracious</kanji>.
雅.on: The crumb is from a slice of <sound>ga</sound>rlic bread.
雅.kun: '<sound>Me</sound>?' chirps the sparrow, and flies off across the <sound>ya</sound>rd with a <sound>bee</sound>.

鈴.meaning: A shepherd who has lost her voice gives the flock its <part>orders</part> by jingling: one jingle for 'eat', two for 'home', three for 'wolf!'. All of it comes from one <part>gold</part> <kanji>small bell</kanji> on her wrist.
鈴.on: Far across the hills, the sheep come running at every <sound>rin</sound>g.
鈴.kun: The wolf, scared off, sulks over a <sound>su</sound>shi roll and a sour yu<sound>zu</sound>.

扶.meaning: A tiny tugboat can't drag a giant ship off the rocks alone. A <part>husband</part> on the pier ties the ship's <part>anchor</part> to his rowing boat and rows with all his might beside it. Slowly, together, they pull it free: the ship got its <kanji>aid</kanji>.
扶.on: Afterwards he collapses onto a <sound>fu</sound>ton on deck.
扶.kun: The grateful crew bring him a <sound>ta</sound>rt and a plate of <sound>su</sound>shi.

蚕.meaning: A little <part>insect</part> munches mulberry leaves and dreams of the <part>heavens</part>. It spins itself a shiny, cloud-white cocoon, hoping to float up into the sky. Instead a weaver unwinds its cloud into a pillowcase, and the moth flutters off to find the sky elsewhere: the <kanji>silkworm</kanji>.
蚕.on: The moth lands on a <sound>sun</sound>dae, mistaking the cream for a cloud.
蚕.kun: It chases a <sound>ki</sound>te all afternoon, then naps on a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala.

奴.meaning: A <part>woman</part> at the fair bets nobody can tie a <part>pretzel</part> into a knot with their tongue. A bloke in a flat cap steps up and does it twice, then bows. Nobody knows his name; everyone just calls him 'that <kanji>guy</kanji>'.
奴.on: Next year he does it while riding a <sound>do</sound>lphin.
奴.kun: '<sound>Ya</sound>, easy!' he grins, then sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' and the knot comes undone.

伐.meaning: A knight hangs her cloak on a <part>coat hook</part>, grips her <part>spear</part> and charges the giant oak blocking the castle road. Hack, hack, hack: by sunset the oak tips over with a groan. She is the first knight ever to <kanji>fell</kanji> a tree.
伐.on: A gold <sound>but</sound>ton pops off her armour from the effort.
伐.kun: A <sound>ki</sound>wi bird drops out of the leaves onto a kanga<sound>roo</sound>'s head: to cut.

耗.meaning: A fluffy yak pulls a <part>plough</part> across a hot field, and with every row it sheds a little more <part>fur</part> into the furrows. By autumn the yak is sleek and the field is woolly. Its coat shows a steady <kanji>decrease</kanji>.
耗.on: The farmer trims the woolly field with a lawn <sound>mo</sound>wer.

溝.meaning: Painters on a tall <part>scaffolding</part> knock over a bucket. <part>water drops</part> rain down the boards, gather into one stream and race along the kerb into a narrow channel. A paper boat sails off down the <kanji>gutter</kanji>.
溝.on: It wedges against a dropped ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne.
溝.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat jumps aboard to steer, with a toy <sound>zo</sound>mbie as crew.

漬.meaning: Grandma finds her cucumbers floating in a jar of salty <part>water drops</part> and puts the <part>blame</part> on the cat. The cat blames the dog. A week later the cucumbers are sour and crunchy, and everyone wants the credit for the <kanji>pickling</kanji>.
漬.on: Now grandma guards the jar behind a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld.
漬.kun: When she opens it, the vinegar makes the cat sneeze: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'

崇.meaning: On top of a <part>mountain</part> sits the tiny shrine of an odd <part>religion</part>: its only god is a grumpy marmot. Every morning hikers climb all the way up just to leave it a peanut and bow. They <kanji>adore</kanji> that marmot.
崇.on: One day a <sound>su</sound>perhero flies up with a whole sack of peanuts.
崇.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' sighs the marmot happily, nibbling a <sound>ga</sound>rlic peanut.

婆.meaning: A <part>woman</part> of ninety goes surfing every morning, riding the biggest <part>waves</part> on an old ironing board. Teenagers on the beach line up for her autograph: she's the coolest <kanji>old woman</kanji> alive.
婆.on: Afterwards she grills fish on the beach <sound>ba</sound>rbecue.
婆.kun: A sheep on the dunes cheers her with one long '<sound>Baa</sound>!'

崎.meaning: A <part>mountain</part> got bored of standing still and stuck one long, <part>strange</part> rocky toe out into the sea to test the water. It has been dipping it ever since, and fishermen picnic on the tip of the <kanji>promontory</kanji>.
崎.on: The lighthouse on the toe is locked with a big brass <sound>key</sound>.
崎.kun: A fisherman shares his <sound>sa</sound>lsa with a <sound>ki</sound>wi bird.

燥.meaning: A dragon babysitter lights a tiny <part>fire</part> under the kids' <part>treehouse</part> to keep it cosy, but it's midsummer. Soon the planks curl, the leaves crackle and the lemonade dries to sugar. Sun and fire together <kanji>parch</kanji> everything.
燥.on: The socks on the washing line dry as stiff as a bar of <sound>so</sound>ap.
燥.kun: The kids don't care: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' they whoop, splashing round the paddling pool like <sound>sha</sound>rks: frolicking.

扉.meaning: A fishmonger nails a big <part>fishbone</part> across her shop's <part>door</part> as a knocker. Visitors tap it and the bones ring out like a xylophone. It's the fanciest <kanji>front door</kanji> on the street.
扉.on: One lady knocks with the <sound>hee</sound>l of her shoe instead.
扉.kun: A cat on <sound>to</sound>p of the door eyes the fishbone, while a <sound>bee</sound> eyes the cat's bowl of <sound>ra</sound>men.

隆.meaning: A gardener plants a seedling bursting with <part>life</part> in a flat field, sets a <part>folding chair</part> beside it and plants a little <part>pennant</part> to mark the spot. Every day the ground under the chair swells higher, until the roots have pushed up a giant <kanji>hump</kanji>.
隆.on: Years later the gardener's whole family holds a <sound>reu</sound>nion on top of it.

后.meaning: Standing on a <part>cliff</part> top, a lady in a crown gives one <part>slash</part> of her fan and opens her <part>mouth</part>: the whole army below falls silent. The king hides behind her cape. Everyone knows who really rules: the <kanji>empress</kanji>.
后.on: Then she hands every soldier an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne.
后.kun: Her pet <sound>ki</sound>wi bird dips its cone in <sound>sa</sound>lsa, then hands her the <sound>key</sound>s to the palace.

帥.meaning: In the duck pond army, an old drake ties a <part>towel</part> to a <part>pole</part> and waves it, quacking orders from a wide-open <part>mouth</part>. Two hundred ducklings swim in perfect rows behind him. He is the <kanji>commander</kanji>.
帥.on: He pays each duckling with one wrapped <sound>swee</sound>t.
